One ridiculous mission

Save the buddies. Learn along the way.

Five ways to play turn quick taps into letter recognition, number practice, timing, and a whole lot of slime. It starts gentle, then grows with a kid who wants a real challenge.

  1. 01 Rotten Rescue Rescue your buddies! Ten gooped worlds, a boss at the end of each.
  2. 02 Snack Attack Survive the rush! No finish line, just a high score.
  3. A–Z ABC's Collect A - B - C, all the way to Z.
  4. 1–99 123's Count 1 - 2 - 3, up to 99.
  5. ★ Practice Pick a game to learn — no clock, no fail!

Learning, disguised

Built to feel like a game first

  • Letter recognition and alphabet order, A to Z
  • Counting and number recognition, 1 to 99
  • Gentle early levels that teach while kids play
  • Practice mode with no clock and no fail state

Small-hand approved

Big buttons. Light reading. Zero scary stuff.

  • Large, friendly touch targets
  • Icons and audio lead the way
  • Stars, stickers, treats and buddies to unlock
  • Landscape play on Android phones and tablets

The grown-ups corner

The boring parts matter, too.

Plain answers about names, ads, purchases and data.

💬

No chat or login

No social features and no account credentials. The game uses an anonymous player record.

🦖

Nickname is optional

A filtered leaderboard nickname can be chosen. Please do not enter a child's real name.

▶

Contextual rewarded ad

The revive ad is optional, child-directed and not personalized by interests.

🔒

Grown-up controls

Purchases sit behind a parental gate, and data can be deleted from inside the game.

Where it came from

A four-year-old had one wonderfully weird request.

When my nephew was four, he made one wonderfully weird request: a game called Stay Away From Poison Hotdogs!

That was the whole idea—just a name that made us laugh. Somehow, that little request grew into Rexy, ridiculous hotdogs, and entirely too much green slime.

It was made for him first. Now we hope it makes your family smile, too.
